sources.title: C. P. Burgess, Introduction to Effective Field Theory
sources.locator: The local fixed-order EFT construction is in §2.2.1–2.2.5, printed pp. 21–28, PDF pp. 21–28; the redundant-interaction and leading-EOM field-redefinition argument is in the §2.1 discussion, printed pp. 14–15, equations (21)–(26).

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.2.1–2.2.5, printed pp. 21–28, including the high/low mode split, Wilson action, fixed-order local expansion, and matching example; also read §3's opening operator-dimension and power-counting passage, printed p. 28, PDF p. 28.
source_review.supports: The EFT convention that a fixed low-energy order uses a finite set of local interactions with specified engineering dimensions and coefficients.
source_review.limitations: The scalar example and heuristic locality discussion do not prove finiteness for the locally defined finite jet algebra or the exact invariant quotient; those arguments are supplied locally.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete redundant-interaction argument in §2.1, printed pp. 14–15, equations (21)–(26), including its integration-by-parts example and its order-by-order remainder.
source_review.supports: At a single retained order, a term proportional to the leading variational equation is canceled by an identity-leading field redefinition; total derivatives are removed under the stated boundary convention.
source_review.limitations: The article's concise argument is a source for EFT convention and example, not a proof of the present general finite-jet statement or of quantum measure and LSZ claims.

source_review.read_extent: Read the scalar integration-by-parts and leading-EOM example in §2.1, printed p. 15, equations (25)–(26).
source_review.supports: The toy scalar density used as the worked example of a derivative operator related to lower-derivative interactions.
source_review.limitations: The example is recomputed with the batch's own mostly-plus Minkowski sign, field-weight, compact-support, and coefficient conventions; no coefficient or sign is copied without calculation.

sources.title: Matthias Neubert, Effective Field Theory and Heavy Quark Physics (2004 TASI Lectures)
sources.locator: Read §2, PDF pp. 5–17, including equations (2)–(12) on mode splitting, local operators, engineering dimensions and finite-order truncation, and equations (27)–(29) on leading-EOM operator redundancy.

source_review.read_extent: Read §2, PDF pp. 5–8, equations (2)–(12), including the local-operator sum, coefficient dimensions in units hbar=c=1, and finite truncation by powers of E/M.
source_review.supports: The coefficient-dimension convention and the need to declare a fixed field content, symmetry allowance, dimension, and truncation order before discussing a finite operator set.
source_review.limitations: Naturalness estimates and physical Wilson-coefficient sizes are not adopted; the batch proves finite-dimensionality from its explicit finite generator and positive-weight hypotheses.

source_review.read_extent: Read §2, PDF pp. 11–12, the stated matching procedure's instruction to enumerate gauge-invariant operators allowed by symmetries and its four-fermion example.
source_review.supports: A basis is selected only after symmetries, dimension, field content, and algebraic relations have been fixed.
source_review.limitations: The source's Standard Model operator list does not establish the batch's abstract finite-dimensional quotient or any complete SMEFT classification.

source_review.read_extent: Read §2, PDF pp. 15–17, equations (27)–(29), including the explicit leading Yang–Mills equation-of-motion substitution and resulting four-fermion operators.
source_review.supports: The distinction between equation-of-motion reduction at a stated EFT order and an unrestricted assertion about off-shell correlators.
source_review.limitations: This is a physical operator example, not the local proof of the batch's general action-level proposition or its symmetry-exactness statement.

sources.title: Juan Carlos Criado and Manuel Pérez-Victoria, Field redefinitions in effective theories at higher orders
sources.locator: Read §2, PDF pp. 6–8, equations (2.2)–(2.8), on regulated change of variables, Jacobian, sources and LSZ; §3, PDF pp. 9–12, equations (3.1)–(3.8), on the first-order EOM rule and its higher-order limitation; §5.1, PDF pp. 17–19, equations (5.2)–(5.5), on order-by-order field redefinitions; and Appendix B, PDF pp. 33–34, equations (B.1)–(B.11), checking single versus multiple EOM insertions.

source_review.read_extent: Read §3 and §5.1 in full at the cited equations, including the generated higher-order terms under successive transformations.
source_review.supports: The EOM relation is valid as a first-order coefficient-space relation; at higher orders the actual invertible field redefinition generates additional terms that must be retained.
source_review.limitations: The batch statement is restricted to an explicit finite-order truncation and proves the Taylor expansion locally; it does not identify an exact nonlinear action with only its linear EOM term.

source_review.read_extent: Read §2, PDF pp. 6–8, and Appendix B, PDF pp. 33–34, including the finite-regulator change-of-variables identity, transformed source/Jacobian, LSZ interpolator argument, and the explicit multiple-insertion counterexample.
source_review.supports: For local perturbative invertible redefinitions, the regulated generating functional remains equal when the Jacobian and source transformation are retained, and LSZ-normalized amplitudes agree for stable external particles with nonzero one-particle overlap; one EOM insertion vanishes on shell at linear order, while multiple insertions need not.
source_review.limitations: The batch theorem states these regulator, measure, pole, stability, and residue hypotheses explicitly. It does not claim a continuum limit, an unaccounted Jacobian is trivial, or off-shell Green-function equality under unchanged sources.

source_review.read_extent: Read the explicit one-insertion and two-insertion on-shell comparison in Appendix B, PDF pp. 33–34.
source_review.supports: The example's boundary between first-order EOM reduction and higher-order corrections.
source_review.limitations: The batch example independently evaluates a six-dimensional scalar operator relation and does not reproduce the paper's diagram calculation.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete stated clauses and proof of reductive-group complete reducibility in Theorem 1.23 and the natural Reynolds projection and surjectivity-on-invariants argument at the start of Theorem 1.24, printed pp. 8–9.
